metadata.dataset_label: Microcosm UK 2024-25, national line from microcosm main c5a1cba8 (staged build)
metadata.dataset_producer: microcosm build uk-frs-calibration-attempt-20260930T155755Z-f8182725 (tools/build_uk_rowwise_candidate.py --release-role national on microcosm main c5a1cba8, the PolicyEngine/microcosm#1045 merge, with policyengine-uk 2.100.0), staged 2026-09-30 in the Hugging Face dataset repo policyengine/populace-uk-private (commit 1b295f37); all seven calibration-seam gates passed, as did microcosm's evaluation against the Enhanced FRS; a staging build, not a certified release
metadata.dataset_observation: FRS 2024-25 spine; capital gains amounts redrawn from HMRC Table 3 (size of gain by taxable income, 2024-25) with asset types from HMRC Tables 7 and 8, gains qualifying for Business Asset Disposal Relief and Investors' Relief imputed from HMRC Table 4, and gain carriers conditioned on wealth through a mass-conserving support split (microcosm#1045); the sub-exempt remainder drawn from the Advani-Summers within-band distribution (microcosm#970); household weights calibrated to 1,090 targets for 2024-25, among them HMRC's CGT totals, size bands, age, region, gains by taxable income band (Table 3) and the BADR bands (Table 4)
metadata.dataset_notes: The build's projection gate (uk_cgt_projection_entrants, run on policyengine-uk 2.100.0) counts 6.7k gainers that uprating carries over the frozen exempt amount by 2030, against HMRC's 73k taxpayers with gains of £3,000 to £5,999 in 2024-25 (Table 2.1a); this repo's uprating audit counts 6.9k on policyengine-uk 2.104.0.
metadata.dataset_columns: It carries capital_gains, capital_gains_residential_property (the residential schedule) and capital_gains_badr (gains qualifying for Business Asset Disposal Relief or Investors' Relief), and no carried-interest column.

rules.not_modelled: Investors' Relief, which CenTax's Table 3 also abolishes, shares the engine's BADR input (capital_gains_badr): it is charged at the BADR rate within the BADR lifetime limit and withdrawn with it; its own £10m limit is not modelled. On a dataset without BADR gains the relief settings are inert.

external.source: CenTax, Reforming Capital Gains Tax: revenue and distributional effects (Advani, Lonsdale and Summers)
external.scope: Equalisation with income tax rates (20/40/45, gains stacked on income), one rate for all assets: BADR, Investors' Relief and the separate residential and carried-interest rates abolished; principal private residence relief kept
external.note: 2019/20 rules and data: main rates 10/20, residential and carried interest 18/28, BADR 10%, exempt amount £12,000; resident individuals; CGT and income tax counted together

external_regions.source: CenTax, Reforming Capital Gains Tax: revenue and distributional effects (Advani, Lonsdale and Summers)
external_regions.scope: Equalisation with income tax rates (20/40/45, gains stacked on income), one rate for all assets: BADR, Investors' Relief and the separate residential and carried-interest rates abolished; principal private residence relief kept

centax_package_context.source: PolicyEngine derivation from CenTax, Reforming Capital Gains Tax: revenue and distributional effects (Advani, Lonsdale and Summers)
centax_package_context.scope: Equalisation with income tax rates (20/40/45, gains stacked on income), one rate for all assets: BADR, Investors' Relief and the separate residential and carried-interest rates abolished; principal private residence relief kept
centax_package_context.note: Not a CenTax figure. CenTax adds the death-uplift (£1.3bn) and exit-charge (£4.3bn) components without a behavioural response; subtracting them from the no-allowance package (£13.8bn, Table 4) leaves about £8.2bn for rates alone. CenTax expects a rates-only reform to face a higher elasticity than its package.

centax_package_context.source: CenTax, Reforming Capital Gains Tax: revenue and distributional effects (Advani, Lonsdale and Summers)
centax_package_context.scope: Package: equalisation plus a rate-of-return investment allowance, removal of the death uplift, and rebasing on arrival with a deemed disposal on departure
centax_package_context.price_basis: nominal, scaled to the OBR's 2025/26 CGT forecast
centax_package_context.note: The headline £14bn: a medium-term effect on the 2025/26 base.

centax_package_context.source: CenTax, Taxes at the top: understanding what high earners pay (Advani, Hughson and Summers)

ready_reckoner.source: HMRC, Direct effects of illustrative tax changes (ready reckoner), June 2025
ready_reckoner.locator: Capital gains tax rows; notes 13 and 14
ready_reckoner.measure: Exchequer receipts in £m (positive = yield), including income tax and SDLT effects, for a change from April 2026 on the OBR's March 2025 forecast
ready_reckoner.note: The higher-rate rows move the higher and additional rates together, for main and residential gains (note 13); rows are non-linear and must not be scaled (note 14). The BADR rows raise the relief's rate from its 18% in 2026-27. HMRC deferred the 2026 edition on 6 July 2026 pending a review of key assumptions, so these rows are provisional.

excluded.reason: A lower rate above the higher rate breaks the explorer's ordering rule.
The explorer changes rates and the relief, not the exempt amount.

ready_reckoner.model_measure: Change in government balance, £m, on this repo's liabilities in the model year, with each row's rates and relief (the main and residential rates move together; the BADR rows move the relief's rate), the official case applying 3.6 to main-rate gains and 1.4 to gains qualifying for the relief
